_help: Act 9 start: Noura al-Khatib and Omar Saqr, the last two guardians (noura_alive, omar_alive: act9.gd clears them when they die; both dead = the rite fails). Omar hates you if you fought the Keepers on the road (recognized_bandits); answering him wins some trust, mocking them costs it. Generated by tools/dialogue/make_act89.py.

start.speaker: noura
start.line: You came back. With it. God is merciful after all. I am Noura al-Khatib; this is Omar Saqr. We are what is left of the Keepers at Akmentar.

omar_hates.speaker: omar
omar_hates.line: I know you. You fought my brothers on the way here, and they died on your guns. I will walk beside you because she asks it. Nothing more.

omar_cold.speaker: omar
omar_cold.line: The foreigner who opened the door. Now he wants to close it. Good. Then hurry.

rashad.speaker: noura
rashad.line: My uncle's rite held him here as long as it could. When it broke he went after the amulet, and my uncle fell, and most of the others with him. We know the binding rite. We need the amulet, the jars, and our lives, until it is done.

menu.speaker: noura
menu.line: Ask, if you must. But walk while you ask.

choices.label: Answer Omar
choices.line: Your brothers shot first, Omar. But I'm sorry for every one of them.

choices.label: Mock their beliefs
choices.line: Your 'rite' had better work better than your rifles did.

choices.label: Go
choices.line: Then let's go. Stay close to me, both of you.

rite.speaker: noura
rite.line: Two voices, one at each end of the altar, while the eye is laid back in its cradle. One voice can do it, if the other falls. Slowly. Too slowly, perhaps.

omar_answer.speaker: omar
omar_answer.line: ...Sorry. Yes. Well. Keep your gun pointed at the dead, and we will see.

mock.speaker: omar
mock.line: Say that again in the burial chamber, foreigner.

go.speaker: noura
go.line: Down, then. Through the ruins, the halls, the king's own door. Whatever you learned here before, use it now.
